reports.title: Scholar Rock Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Business Highlights

desk.headline: First ISEMBYLD sales of $0.6m and a $0.81 loss per share, both better than estimates; no financial guidance

other.label: Priority review voucher sale
other.change: agreed in November, cash on closing

results: The FDA approved ISEMBYLD for spinal muscular atrophy on 11 September; first stock shipped to pharmacies brought in $0.6m of sales.
The net loss widened slightly to $107.2m, but the loss per share fell to $0.81 from $0.90 because more shares are in issue.
Cash and investments were $413.6m, and a deal to sell the priority review voucher will add $205m once it closes.
The European application was resubmitted and accepted, with an opinion due in H1 2027; Japan accepted its filing for priority review.

guidance.summary: Scholar Rock gives no sales or spending guidance and said it would not put numbers on Q4 sales or patient sign-ups. It expects a European opinion in H1 2027 and SRK-439 trial data by the end of 2026.

points: Management said demand is "outpacing reimbursement and access at this stage."
More than a third of the top 140 SMA centres have signed up first patients, and outreach has reached over 95% of them.
Getting from prescription to first infusion takes 60–90 days or more, so most patients signed up by October should start in 2027.
A product-specific billing code is expected on 1 April 2027, and insurers covering about 47m people already have policies.
With the voucher sale and $150m of unused debt, management said it does not need to raise equity now.
